item.title: Defending champions Labasa drawn in tough pool in BOG
item.description: Defending champions Labasa will face Nasinu, Suva and Navua in Pool A of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament. Pool B features Extra Premier League champions Ba, along with Rewa, Lautoka and Nadi.
item.content:encoded:
Defending champions Labasa will face Nasinu, Suva and Navua in Pool A of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament.

Pool B features Extra Premier League champions Ba, along with Rewa, Lautoka and Nadi.

The Battle of the Giants pool matches will be held from 4th to 6th September, with the semi-finals and final taking place on the 12th and 13th at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.

item.title: RKS U14 steps up preparations for Deans semi final clash
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/08/2026 The Ratu Kadavulevu School Under-14 side are determined to make it to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final as they continue preparations for their semi final clash against Ratu Navula College this Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/08/2026

The Ratu Kadavulevu School Under-14 side are determined to make it to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final as they continue preparations for their semi final clash against Ratu Navula College this Saturday.

Head Coach Waisake Matanavou says this week has been about improving their set piece plays and defence because this is an area they feel that they fell short on against Suva Grammar School last week.

Matanavou says they have done their homework and the boys are looking forward to the semi finals this Saturday.

Even though RKS will not be playing in the Under-18 semi-finals, they will be banking on four of their teams participating this week.

The Under-14 grade will face Ratu Navula College at 8.30am at Churchill Park.

The Under-15 side will meet Queen Victoria School at 9.30am while the Under-17 team will take on Ba Methodist High School at 12pm at the HFC Bank Stadium.

The Under-19 side will face Navatu Secondary School at 1.50pm at Buckhurst Park.

Meanwhile, in the Under-18 semi-finals, Grammar will meet Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park, and Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at the HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: U.S. coaches in Fiji to develop flag football ahead of 2028 Olympics
item.description: Fijian students and coaches will have a chance to learn flag football as the U.S. Embassy in Suva has brought two American coaches to Fiji for a week-long program to teach the sport in Suva and Nadi. Flag football is a fast-growing, non-contact variant of American football where defenders stop the ball carrier by pulling fabric flags off their waist belt instead of tackling them to the ground.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian students and coaches will have a chance to learn flag football as the U.S. Embassy in Suva has brought two American coaches to Fiji for a week-long program to teach the sport in Suva and Nadi.

Flag football is a fast-growing, non-contact variant of American football where defenders stop the ball carrier by pulling fabric flags off their waist belt instead of tackling them to the ground.

Typically played 5-on-5, the sport emphasizes speed, agility, and passing.

The program has been organised in partnership with United States of America Football and the U.S. Department of State and aims to build local coaching skills and expand the sport in Fiji ahead of flag football's official debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.

U.S. U17 Girls flag national team head coach Joshua Saunders says Fiji is the best environment to introduce flag football because rugby is deeply rooted in the country, with talented people in sports.

He says the players have good hand-eye coordination and are fast, aggressive and smart.

Saunders says therefore, flag football would be a very easy transition for them.

He says the players they have encountered so far have been very athletic, coachable and willing to learn.

item.title: OFC Men’s Champions League: Rewa FC face must-win clash against Lae City
item.description: Rewa FC coach Tevita Waranaivalu says their final OFC Men’s Champions League group match against Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea will be their most important game as they fight for a place in the semi-finals. Speaking after their 4-2 victory over the Cook Islands’ Tupapa Maraerenga, Waranaivalu says the team knows they need to win the match to keep their campaign alive.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC coach Tevita Waranaivalu says their final OFC Men’s Champions League group match against Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea will be their most important game as they fight for a place in the semi-finals.

Speaking after their 4-2 victory over the Cook Islands’ Tupapa Maraerenga, Waranaivalu says the team knows they need to win the match to keep their campaign alive.

Waranaivalu is also calling on Rewa supporters, particularly those from Nausori and Suva, to travel to Ba in numbers for Saturday’s match.

He says with the game falling on a weekend, fans should take the opportunity to get behind the team.

Rewa FC will face Lae City FC in their third and final group match at 3pm on Saturday at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

They need to win the match to qualify for the semi-finals.
